transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2025-07-09 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Chen (Horizon Infra Lead), Sofia Alvarez (Horizon ML), Priya Patel (Horizon SecOps), Ethan Brooks (Horizon Product)

Summary: quick sync on network incident during canary, status of pilot on private VPC, plan for kernel/CUDA upgrade, perf numbers from last run, next steps.

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll do a quick 45 min sync, prioritize the canary incident, perf, then next steps
00:18 Marcus: cool thanks, yes we saw that brief spike last night, around 10:42pm our side, a handful of requests timed out during the canary switch to the new model variant
00:32 Priya (SE): right we dug in, it looks like the envoy sidecar on your worker pool hit a short-lived connection storm to the Redwood private endpoint, traced to NAT port exhaustion on the subnet gateway
00:46 Sofia: ah that explains the errors in the logs, we saw a bunch of "connection reset" and then retries, some requests collapsed
01:05 Jordan: good find, Marcus can you confirm how many ephemeral ports you have assigned on the NAT gateway and whether you have connection tracking limits?
01:21 Marcus: we are using the default NAT instance with conntrack defaults, I don't think we bumped conntrack. We'll check, but that could be it. Also we saw a regressed p95 at ~220ms for some bursts, normally it's around 110-140ms
01:40 Priya (SE): the timing lines up — during the canary we had a slight increase in concurrent connections due to shorter-lived backend retries. Two mitigations: increase conntrack and enable connection reuse on the envoy sidecar, and we can also route traffic through the dedicated private endpoint to reduce NATs
02:15 Priya Patel (SecOps): any impact on TLS cert rotation or KMS calls during that window? we didn't see KMS failures but want to confirm audit logs are intact
02:30 Jordan: no KMS errors on our side; Redwood's control plane logged the requests. We'll bundle the audit entries and timestamp ranges for you.
02:46 Ethan (Product): on the kernel/driver upgrade — what's the risk window? Marcus asked earlier about CUDA and cuDNN compat for our current boxes
03:00 Priya (SE): we tested the patched runtime on a dev instance — CUDA 12.1 + driver 535 works with our runtime. We did a quick run with the quantized 4-bit model and didn't see accuracy regressions. The main ops are a planned node reboot and driver install, so we recommend a rolling upgrade with one availability zone at a time
03:24 Marcus: that sounds good. Do you have an expected downtime per node?
03:35 Priya (SE): a node reboot for the upgrade is roughly 12-15 minutes visible to running inferences on that node, but because of our routing and automatic fallback to other nodes, end-user impact is minimal if we stage it. During the canary we observed a small spike because the agent retries were aggressive
04:02 Jordan: we should schedule a maintenance window when load is low; Jordan to propose windows after Marcus shares peak hours
04:18 Sofia: quick perf note — we tested batch sizes 1 and 4, p50 is stable, p95 jumps with occasional spikes around 220ms. We think adjusting kv cache warmup and allowing persistent connections will lower the tail
04:36 Priya (SE): exactly — enabling persistent KV cache and prefix dedupe helped in our lab runs. We'll send a config diff you can apply to the sidecar to reduce chattiness
04:55 Marcus: for the VPC peering route tables, we had a small misconfiguration where a secondary subnet wasn't propagated; that's fixed, but we'll share the topology diagram so Redwood can confirm there are no overlapping ranges
05:15 Jordan: please share the diagram, Priya (SE) will validate and confirm whether route propagation could cause asymmetric routing which might explain the timeouts
05:30 Priya Patel (SecOps): security Q — for PHI we need HSM-backed KMS and customer-managed keys. Are those supported in the private deployment?
05:47 Priya (SE): yes, Redwood Private supports KMS integrations and can work with HSM-backed providers; we have a customer-managed keys flow. Jordan will attach the SOC2 and KMS docs after the call
06:05 Ethan: also ask about audit log retention — we need 1 year of immutable logs for compliance
06:18 Jordan: Redwood can provide longer retention as an add-on; I'll include options and costings in the follow-up
06:31 Sofia: one more item — model rollouts: can we do a canary at 5% and then auto-rollback on quality regressions? we want to tie to a delta in eval metrics
06:47 Priya (SE): rollout policies support percent-based canaries and automatic fallback policies. For quality regressions we'd integrate your eval harness and webhook alerts; we can help wire that up in the POC
07:05 Marcus: for the perf tests we'll run tonight we'll include synthetic load and the mixed traffic from our prod-like dataset, expect logs in the shared S3
07:20 Jordan: perfect — please tag the logs with the timeframe and the canary ID. We'll run correlation on our side and check for connection resets and retries
07:36 Priya (SE): also, small tuning: set envoy's keepalive to 60s and reuse connections; increase conntrack to 262144 on your NAT gateway; that combination reduced our error window in the lab
07:58 Marcus: noted, will apply in dev then prod if green
08:12 Priya Patel (SecOps): confirm that audit trails include per-request user identifiers; we need mapping to our internal user IDs for investigations
08:26 Jordan: yes we can include that metadata in the audit logs, we'll show an example export
08:40 Ethan: any blockers from Redwood side for the upgrade?
08:50 Priya (SE): scheduling only; we need agreed window and a brief smoke test post-upgrade. Also will need to validate the model binary compatibility with the upgraded runtime on your hardware
09:05 Marcus: we'll schedule maintenance tentatively the week of 2025-07-21 and confirm next Wednesday
09:20 Jordan: great, we'll follow up with the topology and SOC2/KMS docs by Monday. Priya will send the envoy diff and config suggestions.
09:35 Sofia: thanks, that helps. Anything else?
09:43 Jordan: quick recap of next steps and owners, then we'll close

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors present; product names sometimes mistranscribed (e.g., cuDNN -> cudn), speaker overlaps in two places near 04:36 and 07:36.

End of transcript.
